paragraphs.zh: Figure 3. One X-ray powder diffractogram, the only plot on the sheet. Printed axis labels: the horizontal axis is captioned "2-Theta" (capital T, hyphen, no unit symbol and no "degrees" printed anywhere on the sheet); the vertical axis is captioned "Intensity (CPS)", set vertically and reading bottom to top. The horizontal axis runs left to right from 2 to 40, with labelled ticks at 2, 10, 20, 30 and 40 and unlabelled minor ticks at every whole unit between them (39 ticks in all, one per unit). The vertical axis is a bare line: it carries its caption but no tick marks and no numeric scale at all, so no intensity value can be read off the sheet; it runs bottom to top with intensity increasing upward. The trace is a single continuous scan from 2 to 40 with sharp, well resolved reflections on a low flat background. Roughly 50 separate maxima are distinguishable above the background; about 23 of those are unambiguous peaks and about 15 are strong. One peak dominates, about 2.5 times the height of the next tallest, and it has a distinctly shorter close companion immediately to its right; the tallest reflection lies between the 20 and the 30 tick, nearer the 20 end. At the extreme low-angle edge, next to the 2 tick, the trace rises off the top of the plotted frame and coincides with the drawn vertical axis line; that rise is low-angle scatter running off scale, not a resolved reflection. No 2-theta values were read off the plot: none are printed on the sheet and the peak positions belong to the tables in the body. The sheet does not name which crystalline form the pattern belongs to; the caption is the bare words "Figure 3" and nothing else.

paragraphs.notes: Marker is the figure caption exactly as printed on the sheet, checked on the image at high magnification: "Figure 3", capital F, lower case "igure", the digit 3, no full stop, no form name, no sub-label such as (a) or (b). The digit is unmistakably a 3 and not a 2: it has the flat serifed upper terminal and open double bowl of a 3 in this serif face. This sheet carries exactly ONE plot and ONE caption. There is no second figure on it, no second caption, and no caption that the OCR dropped: an ink-density scan of every row of the page finds text only in five bands, being the running header, the words "Figure 3", the plot itself, the row of x-axis tick labels, and the words "2-Theta". Everything above the caption and below "2-Theta" is blank paper. So on this sheet, Figure 2 does not appear; where Figure 2 is, if it exists, cannot be answered from p03 and is not guessed here. zh and en hold the same English text, since the source language is English and this is a described plot rather than transcribed prose; no normalisation was applied. There is a stray ink dot on the sheet, about 3 by 2 pixels at roughly 45 percent of the way along the axis, floating high above the trace and not connected to it. It sits at about the height of the tallest peak and a naive reader or an automated peak-picker could take it for a peak. It is a scan speck, not a reflection: the columns either side of it are empty from the caption down to the trace.

notes: This is drawing sheet 2 of 2. The schema's doc_part enum (front_page, claims, description) has no value for a drawing sheet, so doc_part is recorded as "drawings", which is what the page is. drawings is [] as a finding, not an omission: the sheet carries an X-ray powder diffractogram and no chemical structure at all, no formula, no scheme, no substituent label, nothing for the structures gate to read. The whole sheet is one plot, its two axis captions, its x-axis tick labels, the caption "Figure 3" and the running header. Nothing on the sheet is illegible. The one thing that cannot be recovered is intensity in absolute terms, because the vertical axis has no numeric scale printed; that is an absence on the page and not a failure of this read. Peak positions were deliberately not estimated off the plot, per the brief; the printed values live in the tables in the body. Text layer cross-check: /tmp/us2010/page03.txt holds 93 characters, being the running header, "Figure 3", and nothing else. It drops both axis captions entirely, so "2-Theta" and "Intensity (CPS)" reach downstream only through this pass. The layer's "Figure 3" agrees with the image, checked digit by digit rather than assumed, because this layer reads the digit 1 as a lower case l on the companion sheet. Read by Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) from runs/US20100041557A1/input/pages/p03.png, with pixel measurements of the axis ticks, the row ink profile and the peak profile made with PIL to keep the tick count and the peak count from being eyeballed.
